name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
description: The largest of Seoul's five Joseon-era royal palaces, with grand throne halls, a lotus-pond pavilion and the Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony at the main gate.
bestTime: Spring or autumn mornings. Entry is free if you wear hanbok. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Changdeokgung Palace & Secret Garden
description: A UNESCO-listed palace that follows the natural landscape, famous for its tranquil Huwon (Secret Garden) of ponds and pavilions.
bestTime: Autumn foliage in late October. Book the Secret Garden tour ahead. Closed Mondays.

name: Deoksugung Palace
description: A compact palace in the city centre where traditional halls stand beside Western-style stone buildings, next to the leafy Deoksugung stone-wall road.
bestTime: Late afternoon into evening when the palace is lit up. Closed Mondays.

name: Bukchon Hanok Village
description: Hillside lanes packed with hundreds of traditional hanok houses between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung, with views over the old city rooftops.
bestTime: Weekday mornings. Visiting hours are 10:00–17:00 because people live here, so keep quiet.

name: National Museum of Korea
description: Korea's flagship museum covering prehistory to the Joseon dynasty, with a serene meditation room for two famous Pensive Bodhisattva statues. Free entry.
bestTime: Any time, a great rainy-day option. Open late on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

photo.credit: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

name: Jogyesa Temple
description: The head temple of Korean Zen Buddhism, right in downtown Seoul, surrounded by ancient trees and colourful lanterns.
bestTime: Around Buddha's Birthday (April–May) for the Lotus Lantern Festival.

name: Bongeunsa Temple
description: A thousand-year-old temple with a giant standing Maitreya Buddha, set against the skyscrapers of Gangnam. Offers short temple-stay programs.
bestTime: Early morning or around Buddha's Birthday.

name: Bukhansan National Park
description: Granite peaks on Seoul's northern edge. The climb to Baegundae summit (836 m) rewards you with sweeping views of the whole city.
bestTime: October for autumn colours. Start early and bring water.
transport: Gupabal Station (Line 3), Exit 1, then bus 704 to Bukhansanseong

photo.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Geomr~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
description: An 11 km restored stream running below street level through downtown, perfect for an evening walk with lights and stepping stones.
bestTime: Evenings, and November for the Seoul Lantern Festival.

name: Yeouido Hangang Park
description: Seoul's favourite riverside park for picnics, bike rentals, fried-chicken deliveries and the spring cherry blossom road.
bestTime: Early April for cherry blossoms; summer evenings for the night markets.

name: Gwangjang Market
description: One of Korea's oldest markets and a street-food paradise: crispy bindaetteok mung-bean pancakes, mayak gimbap and fresh yukhoe.
bestTime: Lunch or early evening. Many stalls close on Sundays.

name: Namdaemun Market
description: A sprawling traditional market near Sungnyemun Gate, known for hotteok, kalguksu alley, and cheap clothes, kitchenware and souvenirs.
bestTime: Weekday mornings to mid-afternoon. Quieter on Sundays.

name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Street
description: Narrow alleys of 1920s hanok converted into trendy cafés, bakeries and restaurants. One of Seoul's most photogenic food spots.
bestTime: Weekday afternoons to avoid long queues.

name: Myeongdong
description: Seoul's busiest shopping district for K-beauty and fashion, which turns into a street-food market every evening.
bestTime: From 17:00 when the street-food stalls open.

name: Insadong
description: A street of traditional craft shops, tea houses and galleries, including the spiral Ssamziegil mall. Good for souvenirs.
bestTime: Sunday afternoons when the main street is car-free.

name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
description: Zaha Hadid's futuristic curved landmark hosting exhibitions and a rose LED garden, surrounded by late-night fashion malls.
bestTime: After dark for the lights and the media façade show.
transport: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station (Lines 2, 4 & 5), Exit 1

name: N Seoul Tower
description: Seoul's iconic tower on Namsan mountain with a 360° observatory, love-lock terraces and the best city views.
bestTime: Sunset into night. Take the Namsan cable car or hike up.
transport: Myeongdong Station (Line 4), Exit 3, then walk to the Namsan cable car

name: Lotte World Tower & Seoul Sky
description: Korea's tallest building (555 m) with a glass-floored observatory, a huge mall, an aquarium and Seokchon Lake next door.
bestTime: Clear days near sunset. Lake cherry blossoms in early April.

name: Starfield Library (COEX)
description: A free public library inside COEX Mall with 13 m-tall bookshelves, one of Seoul's most photographed interiors.
bestTime: Weekday mornings for fewer crowds.
transport: Bongeunsa Station (Line 9), Exit 7, or Samseong Station (Line 2), Exit 5

name: Hongdae
description: The youthful area around Hongik University known for street buskers, indie shops, clubs and photo booths.
bestTime: Friday or Saturday evenings for live street performances.

name: Seongsu-dong
description: Seoul's 'Brooklyn': old factories turned into concept stores, pop-up shops and specialty coffee roasters, next to Seoul Forest.
bestTime: Weekend afternoons for the latest brand pop-ups.

name: Haeundae Beach
description: Korea's most famous beach: a 1.5 km curve of sand backed by skyscrapers, with the Dongbaekseom island walk at its western end.
bestTime: June–August for swimming; the Sand Festival in late May or early June.

name: Gwangalli Beach
description: A lively beach facing the illuminated Gwangan Bridge, lined with cafés and seafood restaurants. Hosts a drone light show on Saturday nights.
bestTime: Saturday evenings for the drone show; November for the Busan Fireworks Festival.

name: Taejongdae
description: Dramatic sea cliffs, a lighthouse and pine forest at the southern tip of Yeongdo island. Ride the Danubi tour train around the loop.
bestTime: Clear days, when you can sometimes see Japan's Tsushima Island.
transport: Nampo Station (Line 1), then bus 8, 30 or 66 to Taejongdae

name: Haeundae Blueline Park
description: Colourful sky capsules and a beach train running along the coastal railway from Mipo to Cheongsapo and Songjeong.
bestTime: Sunset. Book sky capsule tickets online in advance.
transport: Jung-dong Station (Line 2), Exit 7, walk to Mipo Station

name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
description: A rare seaside temple built on rocks right above the crashing waves, especially beautiful at sunrise.
bestTime: Early morning before tour buses arrive; Buddha's Birthday for lanterns.
transport: OSIRIA Station (Donghae Line), then bus 139 or a 20-minute walk

name: Beomeosa Temple
description: A major mountain temple on Geumjeongsan, founded in 678, with forest trails leading up to Geumjeong Fortress.
bestTime: Spring and autumn; combine with a hike on Geumjeongsan.

name: Jagalchi Fish Market
description: Korea's largest seafood market. Choose your fish downstairs and have it prepared as fresh sashimi upstairs.
bestTime: Morning for the liveliest market; lunch for raw-fish platters.

name: Gukje Market & BIFF Square
description: A huge post-war market of alleys selling everything, next to BIFF Square's film-star handprints and famous seed-filled ssiat hotteok.
bestTime: Afternoon into evening when the food stalls are busiest.
transport: Jagalchi Station (Line 1), Exit 7, or Nampo Station, Exit 1

name: Shinsegae Centum City
description: Once the world's largest department store, with a hot-spring spa (Spa Land), cinemas and an ice rink under one roof.
bestTime: Rainy days, or relax at Spa Land after a day of walking.

name: Gamcheon Culture Village
description: A hillside of pastel-painted houses, street art and winding stairs, nicknamed the 'Machu Picchu of Busan'.
bestTime: Morning light. Pick up a stamp-trail map at the information centre.
transport: Toseong Station (Line 1), Exit 6, then village bus 2 or 2-2

name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
description: White houses on a seaside cliff in Yeongdo with cafés overlooking ships at anchor, a filming spot for the movie 'The Attorney'.
bestTime: Sunset, then walk the coastal tunnel path below.
transport: Nampo Station (Line 1), then bus 7, 71 or 508 to Huinnyeoul

name: Busan Tower & Yongdusan Park
description: A tower in hilltop Yongdusan Park with panoramic views of the port, Nampo-dong and Yeongdo Bridge.
bestTime: Evening for city lights; reach it by escalators from Gwangbok-ro.
